The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of the mother tongue in the education system is a powerful symbol of local agency and of the desire to make education more meaningful to the children of Burkina Faso and their families.
the development of bilingual programs in Africa is a complex and contested process, and that there is no single model which is appropriate for all contexts.
the development of a bilingual education model in francophone Africa requires a careful consideration of local needs and resources.
